title: the type-argument door is a roster of members admitting a class or an inline shape, and the diagnostic names both
scope:
what a call site may write between the angle brackets of a compiler-owned member that
declares a type variable it cannot infer, and which members have that door. Not in scope: the members
themselves, whose rosters are [docs/spec/01-core-library.md](../spec/01-core-library.md) §§ 6, 15 and
18, and the hydration walk a shape argument runs, which is [0157](0157.md)'s type surface and
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/json.rs`'s module doc.
dependsOnText:
[0007](0007.md) § 5 — the door itself, and why user-written generics are not part of
it; [0036](0036.md) — the inline shape type; [0157](0157.md) — the optional key and the qualifier
that made a shape worth writing there.

summary.headline: A decoding member takes a class or an inline shape as its type argument
summary.body:
`Core\Json::decodeAs<User>`, `Core\Db::queryAs<User>` and `Core\Request::jsonAs<User>` build a
typed value straight from text, and the type written in the angle brackets may be a class, an
inline shape such as `{id: int, name: string}`, or an array of either. A shape works there
because it declares its own fields on the spot, so nothing has to be looked up elsewhere. Which
members offer the angle brackets is a table the compiler holds, so adding one is a row, not a
language change.
